text.p: Italian debt markets soared to new heights on Wednesday, boosted by lira strength against the mark, as the conviction grew that a tough budget will generate enough momentum to carry Italy into a currency union by 1999.

"Everyone is buying the idea of Italy in EMU and of economic convergence," said a London-based futures trader. "The idea is that Italy will come close to qualifying for EMU on time even if it does not make it."

Italy has to narrow its public sector deficit-to-GDP ratio to three percent by end-1997 if it is to qualify as a founder member of a currency union in 1999. Many economists believe it is practically impossible to meet the three percent target.
"People are banking on the fact that sooner or later Italy is going to join EMU and when that happens the BTP-Bund spread will go to zero," said another London trader with a major European bank.

The bund to BTP spread finished the day at 275 basis points, below a day's high of 272 which dealers said was narrower than it has been at any time since the lira's exit in 1992 from the European exchange rate mechanism.

The market is now widely seen as overbought and ripe for a technical correction but the underpinning remains strong, say dealers. "A technical correction is on the cards but noone is going short at the moment," said the trader.
Italian bonds faltered at the beginning of the week after preliminary inflation figures showed cpi falling more slowly than expected but the market soon shrugged off its disappointment.
Market commentators are confident that with so much at stake for Italy, nobody would like to take on the responsibility of torpedoing Prime minister Romano Prodi's budget plans.
Hard left leader Fausto Bertinotti has said he is opposed to any cuts falling on healthcare or pensions.
